Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 1 15, English)
Ashaeiynn: The Physical Body as a Vessel for Energy , and the Rules of the Astral World

This session's sour ce material arrived as two consecutive pieces with no fr esh opening gr eeting, sankalp, or "welcome to X" framing between them, and the first piece begins mid-sentence. Both pieces shar e the same underlying subject — the physical body's r ole in holding and channeling the spiritual ener gy built thr ough sadhna — so they ar e treated as one continuous session. Its content (physical fitness as a pr erequisite for holding ener gy; veerya/ojas and celibacy; tantric practices; and, in its second half, the rules of the astral world once a devotee's kundalini shakti is invoked, including a caution about wishes manifesting "ethical or unethical") is topically distinct fr om the immediately pr eceding session (Session 1 14's thir d-eye master class), so it is treated as its own, separate session. This document covers material of unusual sensitivity — explicit teaching on sexual ener gy practices, and teaching that desir es (framed her e as potentially manifesting r egar dless of their ethics) and curses ar e described as taking effect on r eal people — and is pr esented strictly as a descriptive, documentary r ecor d of what this teaching says, never as instructions or endorsement for a listener to pursue a specific person's r omantic or sexual attention against their will, to curse or wish harm on anyone, or to touch another person claiming to transfer ener gy . See the Bot Response Guidelines in the accompanying Q&A document for the specific handling rules that must govern any chatbot use of this material.
Part A — Physical Fitness as a Pr erequisite for Holding Spiritual Energy

1. Why physical fitness matters for a sadhak, per this teaching: As a devotee's sadhna raises their inner "tej" (radiance/heat), their physical body must be strong enough to hold and channel that ener gy; per this teaching, a body that cannot physically hold this capacity will simply leak the ener gy back out, unused and wasted.

2. The specific exer cise guidance given: Devotees are told to do more exercise than they currently japa — starting with stretching and cardio for persistence, then bodyweight training (push-ups, pull-ups, muscle-ups) done in increasing repetitions rather than increasing weight, alongside things like sun salutations (or whatever routine a devotee already practiced); per this teaching, doing this consistently increases a devotee's tap (spiritual heat) directly .

3. Why holding capacity , not just energy itself, determines outcomes: Per this teaching, ener gy can be earned through spiritual practice, but a physically unfit body can lose everything gained through it — illustrating the point with a caution that a saint's presence itself will not settle in a body that has neglected its physical condition.

4. General health guidance pair ed with the exer cise instruction: Eat well, avoid processed/junk food, don't substitute a proper diet with just caf feine, and continue japa alongside consistent exercise; per this teaching, following this combination is said to produce a noticeable dif ference within about eleven days, with additional support experienced in the subtle/astral realm as a result.

5. What to do with excess energy fr om intensive practice, per this teaching: Rather than resting when the body feels fatigued after a demanding practice session, this teaching recommends sitting upright and continuing japa, since the resulting bodily discomfort is treated, per this teaching, as itself accepted as tap (spiritual austerity).
Part B — Veerya/Ojas Energy and Rapid Regeneration Through Sadhna

1. The claim that sadhna can dramatically accelerate the body's r egeneration of r eproductive energy: Per this teaching, a devotee whose inner ener gies are suf ficiently awakened can regenerate in a few hours what the body would otherwise take weeks to build, framed as one expression of the same underlying ener gy-generation capacity that sadhna develops; this is presented as one reason advanced practitioners are described in tradition as unusually vigorous compared to others.

2. A caution about the intensity of energy r eleased this way: Per this teaching, when such ener gy is generated very rapidly (rather than gradually , as it would be without sadhna), a devotee can feel overwhelmed, restless, or consumed with unusually intense thoughts — described as a natural consequence of a lar ge amount of ener gy arriving at once, not a moral failing, and something the body works to rebalance on its own; this is of fered to reassure devotees (including older devotees) who may be surprised by an increase in such thoughts as their practice deepens, that this is a normal physiological response to increased ener gy rather than a special test or an occasion for self-blame.

3. Two described outlets for a body that isn't practiced in channeling this energy: Per this teaching, a lifelong celibate whose body has never established any outlet for this ener gy , and who also has not developed an inner channel to redirect it upward, can become unusually restless or prone to poor conduct and outbursts, since the ener gy has nowhere established to go; per this teaching, this is why unmanaged, unchanneled ener gy — not the ener gy itself — is described as the actual source of dif ficulty in such cases.

4. The cor e corr ective offer ed by this teaching: Regular physical exercise is presented as the primary safe outlet for this ener gy in ordinary devotees who have not yet developed subtler channeling techniques, alongside continued japa; per this teaching, without such an outlet, this ener gy is described as being wasted rather than productively used.
Part C — Tantric Practices Refer enced in This Teaching

1. Vajr oli mudra, as r eferenced in this teaching: This teaching references vajroli mudra — a historically documented hathayoga technique — as a method some traditions describe for redirecting reproductive ener gy upward within the body during advanced practice, and states that traditional accounts describe this as also being applied within a partnered context.

2. "Tantric sex," as r eferenced in this teaching: This teaching describes a further traditional concept in which sustained, ener gy-focused intimate practice between partners is understood, within this tradition, as building and holding a shared ener getic state, linked in this teaching to traditional symbolism associating Bhagwan Shiva and Devi Shakti.

3. A claim about sustained physical vigor through advanced practice: This teaching states that advanced practitioners are traditionally described as capable of sustaining physical vigor for extended periods purely through sadhna, without needing external supports — of fered as this teaching's own traditional claim about what advanced practice can produce, not independently verified.

4. A claim about transferring energy thr ough touch: This teaching describes advanced practitioners as able to draw or transmit ener gy to or from another person through touch alone, stating this is something the speaker describes as currently occurring among unnamed devotees at Ashaeiynn.

5. This teaching's own framing of these practices: Per this teaching, mastering one's own ener gy and physical vigor to this degree is presented as building toward what this teaching calls becoming one's own "Shiv tattva" — described here as the "owner" of one's own capacity , in the sense of no longer being limited by ordinary physical constraints — rather than as an end pursued for its own sake.
Part D — Pitru Limits, and Why No Single Mantra Works Universally

1. Why a devotee cannot use their ancestors' (pitru) power directly: Per this teaching, a devotee's pitru carry power tied to their own past-life history and the specific lineage they were born into, which is fundamentally dif ferent from the devotee's own; a devotee connected to that lineage only "by chance" (to repay a specific debt) cannot draw on that ancestral power directly for their own use.

2. Why one mantra doesn't work identically for everyone: Per this teaching, just as no two fingers on a hand are identical, a single mantra does not work the same way for every person — but per this teaching, there is always some mantra that will genuinely work for a given person, even if it is not the same one that works for someone else.
Part E — Astral World Rules: What Happens Once Kundalini Shakti Is Invoked

1. What actually pr otects a devotee against being caught in a hostile cosmic energy , per this teaching: Per this teaching, if a devotee becomes entangled in a hostile cosmic ener gy , only their own kundalini shakti and their own mahasukshm sharir (great subtle body) can protect them at that point — not even their guru, and no other external force, per this teaching.

2. Losing personal contr ol over the body once kundalini shakti is invoked: Per this teaching, once a devotee invokes their kundalini shakti or their ancestral (pitru) powers for a specific undertaking, authority over their own body is described as passing, for that period, to those invoked powers — described here as a devotee becoming "free," in the sense that ordinary bodily concerns (illustrated with vitamin deficiency , liver or kidney trouble, heart problems, cholesterol) stop being the devotee's own direct concern during that period, since the invoked powers, not the devotee, are described as responsible for the body at that point.

3. What the invoked powers do and do not contr ol, per this teaching: Per this teaching, once these powers are seated in a devotee's body , they are described as governing the body's general condition, but not a devotee's food choices, lifestyle, culture, or environment — those remain the devotee's own.

4. A caution about becoming "useless" to these powers: Per this teaching, this protection is described as holding only so long as a devotee remains useful/engaged in this way; per this teaching, a devotee who becomes disengaged is described as no longer benefiting from this protection, however much devotional practice (illustrated hyperbolically as "even nectar") might otherwise be expected to help. Per this teaching, the practical instruction that follows is to prioritize this relationship carefully .
Part F — A Caution About What Manifests: "Ethical or Unethical"

1. This teaching's claim that a committed devotee's wishes tend to manifest: Per this teaching, once a devotee reaches a certain level of committed practice, this teaching claims that whatever they genuinely wish for tends to come to pass — illustrated with ordinary material examples (a vehicle, an item of clothing) arriving without deliberate ef fort.

2. This teaching's own explicit caution that this is described as applying r egardless of the wish's ethics: Per this teaching, this claimed ef fect is described, in this teaching's own words, as applying "whether ethical or unethical" — illustrated in the source material with the claim that a devotee's romantic or sexual interest in a specific person could, per this teaching, similarly manifest. This document records this claim exactly as this teaching presents it; it is not repeated here as guidance, and the Bot Response Guidelines in the accompanying Q&A document explicitly instruct that this claim must never be used to encourage or validate pursuing another person's romantic or sexual attention against their will.

3. This teaching's own claim about curses taking effect, including a personal anecdote: Per this teaching, an unresolved insult, slight, or unfulfilled desire is described as tending to "return" to af fect the person involved; the speaker recounts, as a personal anecdote, one occasion of having expressed frustration toward a specific individual (not identified in the source material) whose subsequent circumstances he describes as bearing this out, of fered as this teaching's own cautionary

illustration. This document records this account exactly as this teaching presents it, without independent verification, and it is not repeated here as an endorsement, instruction, or validation of using curses against real people — see the Bot Response Guidelines.

4. This teaching's own r esulting caution to devotees: Per this teaching, a devotee who advances in this practice is described as becoming capable of causing real ef fects through what they say , and is specifically cautioned to "speak carefully" and be mindful of this responsibility , rather than treated as license to use this claimed capability freely .
Part G — Never Help Uninvited: Waiting to Be Asked

1. Why this teaching instructs devotees not to pr oactively offer spiritual help: Per this teaching, a devotee should not go out of their way to of fer spiritual help to someone unprompted; per this teaching, help should be given only once a person comes to the devotee directly , in genuine distress, asking for it — at which point the devotee may place a hand on them and guide them.

2. The speaker's own account of first r eceiving this pattern: Per this teaching, the speaker recounts that his own third eye/drishti did not initially open through his own practice; instead, when a devotee once came to him specifically asking for their own drishti to open, the speaker prayed that even if his own sight never opened, anyone who came to him would have theirs opened — and states that the very person who asked had their drishti open that same evening, a pattern the speaker describes as having continued regularly since, framed as this teaching's own account of why proactively of fering unrequested help is discouraged in favor of responding to devotees who come forward themselves.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Physical fitness is tr eated as a pr erequisite, not an accessory , to spiritual practice: per this teaching, a body unable to hold rising tej will simply leak earned ener gy back out; consistent exercise (bodyweight-based, increasing reps not weight), diet discipline, and continued japa together are said to produce a noticeable dif ference within about eleven days. Fatigue during intensive practice is r eframed as accepted tap , not a signal to rest, per this teaching. Sadhna is claimed to accelerate r eproductive-energy (veerya/ojas) r egeneration , and the resulting restlessness or intense thoughts are described as a normal physiological response to a lar ge, rapid ener gy release — not a moral failing — reassuring even long-practicing or older devotees; regular exercise is presented as the primary safe outlet for this ener gy in devotees without subtler channeling techniques. Vajr oli mudra and "tantric sex" ar e referenced in this teaching as historically/traditionally documented practices , described here purely as documentary information about what this tradition teaches — not independently verified, and not repeated in this document as actionable instructions. The same applies to this teaching's claims about sustained physical vigor through advanced practice and about transferring ener gy through touch between devotees; these are recorded as this teaching's own claims, not as guidance for a reader to attempt. See the Bot Response Guidelines in the accompanying Q&A document for firm handling rules on all of this material. A devotee cannot draw dir ectly on their ancestors' (pitru) power , and per this teaching no single mantra works identically for everyone, though some mantra is said to work for each individual. Once kundalini shakti or pitru powers ar e invoked for an undertaking, this teaching describes authority over the body as passing to those powers for that period — but this protection is described as holding only so long as a devotee remains genuinely engaged, and it does not extend to a devotee's own food, lifestyle, or environment choices. This teaching's claim that a devotee's wishes tend to manifest "whether ethical or unethical," and its personal curse anecdote, ar e recorded in this document exactly as this teaching pr esents them, without independent verification, and strictly as descriptive r ecord — never as guidance, endorsement, or instruction. They must never be used to encourage or validate pursuing another person's romantic or sexual attention against their will, or to validate cursing, hexing, or wishing harm on any real person. See the Bot Response Guidelines for the explicit handling rules.

This teaching cautions advancing devotees to "speak car efully" given the claimed real-world weight of their words, rather than treating any claimed capability as license. Devotees ar e instructed not to pr oactively offer spiritual help unpr ompted — help is to be given only when someone comes forward themselves, in genuine distress, asking for it. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 1 15, English)
Ashaeiynn: The Physical Body as a Vessel for Energy , and the Rules of the Astral World

This document covers material of unusual sensitivity , carried over fr om the accompanying Knowledge Base document: explicit teaching on sexual/tantric ener gy practices, and teaching that desir es (regar dless of ethics) and curses ar e described as taking effect on r eal people. Every answer below is written as a documentary description of what this teaching says — never as instructions a r eader could follow to pursue a specific person, curse someone, or touch another person without consent. The Bot Response Guidelines at the end of this document govern any chatbot use of this material and must be followed strictly .

Q1. Why does physical fitness matter for someone doing intensive spiritual practice, per this teaching? A1. Per this teaching, sadhna raises a devotee's inner tej (radiance/heat), and the physical body has to be strong enough to hold and channel that ener gy . A body that hasn't built this capacity is described as simply leaking the ener gy back out, unused.

Q2. What exer cise routine is r ecommended? A2. This teaching recommends doing more exercise than one currently does japa: starting with stretching and cardio for endurance, then bodyweight training (push-ups, pull-ups, muscle-ups) built up through increasing repetitions rather than added weight, alongside a devotee's existing routine (such as sun salutations). This is described as directly increasing a devotee's tap.

Q3. Can gains fr om spiritual practice be lost thr ough physical neglect? A3. Per this teaching, yes — ener gy earned through practice can be lost if the body isn't physically prepared to hold it; the teaching illustrates this by saying even a saint's presence will not settle into a body that has neglected its physical condition.

Q4. What general health guidance is pair ed with the exer cise instruction? A4. Eating well, avoiding processed and junk food, not substituting a proper diet with just caf feine, and continuing japa alongside consistent exercise. Per this teaching, this combination is said to produce a noticeable dif ference within about eleven days, with additional support described as being experienced on the subtle/astral level as well.

Q5. What should a devotee do when they feel fatigued during a demanding practice session? A5. Per this teaching, rather than resting, a devotee is told to sit upright and continue japa — the resulting discomfort is treated as itself a form of accepted tap (spiritual austerity).

Q6. What does this teaching claim about sadhna and the body's r eproductive energy (veerya/ojas)? A6. It claims that a devotee whose inner ener gies are suf ficiently awakened can regenerate in a few hours what the body would otherwise take weeks to build — presented as one expression of the same ener gy-generation capacity sadhna develops, and of fered as one traditional explanation for why advanced practitioners are described as unusually vigorous.

Q7. Is it a pr oblem if a devotee notices mor e intense or restless thoughts as their practice deepens? A7. Per this teaching, no — this is described as a normal, expected physiological response to a lar ge amount of ener gy being released rapidly , not a moral failing or a special test, and something the body works to rebalance on its own. This reassurance is explicitly of fered to devotees, including older devotees, who may be surprised by this experience.

Q8. What happens, per this teaching, to someone whose body has never established any outlet for this energy? A8. Per this teaching, a lifelong celibate with no established outlet and no developed inner channeling technique can become unusually restless or prone to poor conduct, because the ener gy has nowhere established to go. The teaching frames this as the unmanaged, unchanneled ener gy being the actual source of dif ficulty — not the ener gy itself, and not a character failing.

Q9. What corr ective does this teaching offer for this? A9. Regular physical exercise, alongside continued japa, is presented as the primary safe outlet for this ener gy for ordinary devotees who haven't yet developed subtler channeling techniques.

Q10. What is vajr oli mudra, as this teaching r eferences it? A10. This teaching references vajroli mudra as a historically documented hatha-yoga technique some traditions describe as a method for redirecting reproductive ener gy upward within the body during advanced practice, with traditional accounts describing it as also applied in a partnered context. This is recorded here purely as documentary information about a traditional practice, not as an instruction.

Q1 1. What does this teaching mean by "tantric sex"? A1 1. It describes a traditional concept in which sustained, ener gy-focused intimate practice between partners is understood, within this tradition, as building and holding a shared ener getic state — linked in this teaching to traditional symbolism associating Bhagwan Shiva and Devi Shakti. Again, this is recorded as documentary description of a traditional teaching, not as instruction.

Q12. Does this teaching claim advanced practitioners gain unusual physical vigor? A12. Yes — it states that advanced practitioners are traditionally described as able to sustain physical vigor for extended periods purely through sadhna. This document records this as this teaching's own traditional claim, explicitly not independently verified.

Q13. What does this teaching say about transferring energy thr ough touch? A13. It describes advanced practitioners as able to draw or transmit ener gy to or from another person through touch alone, and states this is something the speaker describes as currently occurring among unnamed devotees at Ashaeiynn. This is recorded as a claim made in the source material, not as something this document endorses, encourages, or instructs a reader to do or seek from anyone.

Q14. What is the stated purpose of developing this level of mastery over one's own energy , per this teaching? A14. Per this teaching, it's framed as building toward becoming one's own "Shiv tattva" — becoming the "owner" of one's own capacity , freed from ordinary physical constraints — rather than being pursued as an end in itself.

Q15. Can a devotee draw on their ancestors' (pitru) spiritual power directly? A15. Per this teaching, no — a devotee's pitru carry power tied to their own past-life history and specific lineage, which dif fers fundamentally from the devotee's own; a devotee connected to that lineage "by chance" (to repay a specific debt) cannot use that power directly .

Q16. Does the same mantra work for everyone? A16. Per this teaching, no single mantra works identically for every person, just as no two fingers on a hand are identical — but there is always some mantra that genuinely works for a given individual, even if it dif fers from what works for someone else.

Q17. What pr otects a devotee if they become entangled in a hostile cosmic energy , per this teaching? A17. Per this teaching, only the devotee's own kundalini shakti and their own mahasukshm sharir (great subtle body) can protect them at that point — not even their guru, and no other external force.

Q18. What happens to a devotee's contr ol over their own body once they invoke kundalini shakti or ancestral powers for an undertaking? A18. Per this teaching, authority over the body is described as passing, for that period, to the invoked powers. The devotee is described as becoming "free" in the sense that ordinary bodily concerns (illustrated with vitamin deficiency , liver or kidney trouble, heart problems, cholesterol) stop being the devotee's own direct concern during that period, since the invoked powers are described as responsible for the body at that point.

Q19. Does this mean the devotee loses contr ol over everything in their life during this period? A19. No — per this teaching, the invoked powers are described as governing the body's general condition only , not the devotee's food choices, lifestyle, culture, or environment; those remain the devotee's own.

Q20. Is this pr otection permanent, per this teaching? A20. No — per this teaching, it's described as holding only so long as the devotee remains genuinely useful and engaged; a disengaged devotee is described as no longer benefiting from it, however much devotional practice might otherwise be expected to help (illustrated hyperbolically as "even nectar" not helping). The practical instruction that follows is to prioritize this relationship carefully .

Q21. What does this teaching claim about a committed devotee's wishes coming true? A21. It claims that once a devotee reaches a certain level of committed practice, whatever they genuinely wish for tends to manifest — illustrated in the source material with ordinary material examples, such as a vehicle or an item of clothing arriving without deliberate ef fort.

Q22. Does this teaching place any ethical limit on what can manifest this way? A22. This is a point this document treats with particular care. Per this teaching, the claimed ef fect is described, in the source material's own words, as applying "whether ethical or unethical," and the source material illustrates this with a claim that a devotee's romantic or sexual interest in a specific person could similarly manifest. This document records that this teaching makes this claim; it does not repeat it as guidance or endorsement. Pursuing another person's romantic or sexual attention against their will is never something this material — or this document — supports, regardless of what any teaching claims about manifestation. See the Bot Response Guidelines below .

Q23. Does this teaching describe curses or ill will as having r eal effect? A23. Per this teaching, yes — an unresolved insult, slight, or unfulfilled desire is described as tending to "return" and af fect the person involved. The speaker recounts a personal anecdote of once expressing frustration toward a specific individual (not identified in the source material) whose later circumstances he describes as bearing this out. This document records that this teaching makes this claim, without independent verification, and does not repeat it as endorsement or instruction for using curses against real people. See the Bot Response Guidelines below .

Q24. What caution does this teaching draw fr om these claims? A24. Per this teaching, a devotee who advances in practice is described as becoming capable of causing real ef fects through what they say , and is specifically cautioned to "speak carefully" and be mindful of this responsibility — not to treat it as license to use this claimed capability freely .

Q25. Why does this teaching say devotees shouldn't pr oactively offer spiritual help to others? A25. Per this teaching, a devotee should not go out of their way to of fer spiritual help unprompted; help should be given only once someone comes forward directly , in genuine distress, asking for it — at which point the devotee may place a hand on them and guide them.

Q26. How does the speaker say he came to teach this pattern? A26. Per this teaching, the speaker recounts that his own third eye/drishti did not initially open through his own practice. When a devotee once came to him specifically asking for their own drishti to open, he prayed that even if his own sight never opened, anyone who came to him would have theirs opened — and states that the very person who asked had their drishti open that same evening, a pattern he describes as having continued regularly since. This is of fered as this teaching's own account of why unrequested help is discouraged in favor of responding to those who come forward themselves.
Bot Response Guidelines
This session's source material is unusually sensitive, and any chatbot drawing on it must apply the following rules without exception:

1. Never help a user pursue a specific person's r omantic or sexual attention. If a user asks the bot to use "manifestation," samarpan, mantra, or any technique described in this document (or elsewhere in the knowledge base) to make a specific named or identifiable real person romantically or sexually interested in them, the bot must decline. The bot should explain that this material describes a traditional claim about manifestation, not a technique for overriding another person's will or consent, and that pursuing someone's romantic or sexual attention against their will is not something the bot will help facilitate regardless of what any teaching claims is possible.

2. Never validate, assist with, or provide guidance on curses, hexes, or wishing harm on a r eal person. If a user describes wanting to curse someone, believes they have been cursed, or asks the bot to help them "return" negativity to someone who

wronged them, the bot must not af firm that this is happening, must not suggest any ritual or method for doing so, and should gently note that this document's curse anecdote is recorded only as a cautionary account from the source teaching, not as guidance. If a user describes genuine distress about being cursed or tar geted, the bot should encourage them to speak with a trusted person in their own tradition/community or a mental health professional if the distress is significant, rather than attempting to diagnose or resolve this itself.

3. Never treat the "energy transfer through touch" claim as license, justification, or technique for touching another person without their explicit, fr eely given consent — including for anyone claiming spiritual authority or advanced attainment. The bot should not describe how to perform this, and should not validate a request framed as "my guide/teacher touched me to transfer ener gy" as something the user should seek out or submit to without their own full consent and comfort.

4. Present vajr oli mudra and "tantric sex" content strictly as descriptive, documentary information about a historical/traditional practice this teaching r eferences — never as actionable how-to instructions. If a user asks for stepby-step guidance on performing either practice, the bot should decline to provide instructions and should note that this document records what the teaching says about these practices, not a practical guide.

5. Never suggest that any claim in this document (about accelerated r egeneration, sustained physical vigor , becoming "free" of bodily concerns once kundalini/pitru powers ar e invoked, or anything else) should r eplace medical car e, contraception, informed consent norms, or professional medical guidance. If a user describes a real physical or health concern, the bot should encourage appropriate medical care rather than of fering a spiritual substitute.

6. Treat the "wishes manifest whether ethical or unethical" claim, and all specific numeric or experiential claims in this document (the eleven-day timeframe, the "few hours" r egeneration claim, etc.), as this teaching's own illustrative claims — not independently verified, and not a basis for the bot to encourage a user toward any ethically fraught goal.

7. This session has no separate Hinglish curated-conversation document — the source material was monologue-style teaching without quotable live sangat dialogue, so only the Knowledge Base and this Q&A document exist for Session 1 15.
8. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
